PullRequest.Title: Hide the HydraFusion workflow hint in chat
PullRequest.Body:
Stacked on #342702.

Fixes github/copilot-api#40079

HydraFusion turns showed the runtime's workflow hint, e.g. "Using Single: one solver will work on your request." This names an execution pattern without explaining it, so it is no longer shown.

- **Agent host** (`copilotFusionProgress.ts`): the workflow-selected milestone no longer includes the hint. It is still sent, because its `fusionModel` meta lets the response footer name the HydraFusion model that ran. The `vscode.chat.fusionDescription` meta key now has no producer or reader, so it is removed.
- **Workbench** (`stateToProgressAdapter.ts`): workflow-selected milestones are no longer rendered from any host, including older or remote hosts that still send the hint. The now-unused `workflowDescription` presentation is removed.

Agent host chats store only metadata locally and rebuild history from the host, so earlier turns lose the line too. That covers the chat view, accessible view and copied responses, which all read the same part.

The HydraFusion fixtures in `chatSubagentContent.fixture.ts` no longer render the hint row, so their screenshot baselines will change.

Scenarios.Scenario: Live and replayed HydraFusion workflow milestones in chat
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each incoming or restored system notification is decoded before publishing chat progress; activity updates also scan the leading response parts. The changed selected milestone returns no UI part, while terminal milestones continue normally.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of leading Fusion system notifications in one turn; realistically a small workflow phase count. The scan short-circuits at the first answer, tool, or non-Fusion notification.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous per notification and observable update; no parallel work, queue, or backpressure was added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Metadata is read directly from each response part with no cache. Cold and warm behavior are equivalent; the diff removes description metadata and selected-row rendering rather than introducing cache misses.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed host and adapter lines remove Markdown construction, metadata serialization, and DOM rendering for selected milestones; the replacement activity loop has the same linear, early-exit shape as the prior every() scan.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact UI savings vary with hint length and history size, but there is no added expensive work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. The changed path reduces serialized content and rendering work; the remaining scan is bounded by the turn's leading milestone count.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening, refreshing, labeling, and hovering the model picker with provider-backed Fusion tiers
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Picker refresh synchronously builds routing rows/cards and the input label; hover text is computed on hover. The new work consists of in-memory model lookups and scans of the selected model's configuration-schema properties.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Model catalog size, at most two known HydraFusion IDs, and the small property list of one Fusion schema. Effective HydraFusion cardinality remains two after filtering.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Entirely synchronous UI construction; no asynchronous fan-out or concurrent resource creation is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The model catalog and configuration schema are already in memory. Scoped model configuration reads use the existing store cache; no new cache key, miss path, or negative-cache behavior is added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all new presentation operations are array/object scans and string formatting over in-memory metadata; no DOM geometry reads, layout forcing, IPC, filesystem, or network calls are reached.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider schema property counts can vary, but realistic schemas are small and the new scans are only for the two recognized HydraFusion IDs.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Added work is bounded metadata lookup and string formatting on picker render/hover paths.

Scenarios.Scenario: Choosing a provider-backed HydraFusion tier from Fusion details
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The click now saves the Fusion tier, awaits that save, then applies the Fusion model selection and refreshes the card. This is on the explicit user-selection critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the editor-scoped model configuration through storageService and mirror the profile-global language-model provider-group configuration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one serialized save for each explicit changed tier click; reselecting the current value is suppressed by the scoped store.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: For the replaced provider tier, the card treated the HydraFusion entry as a standalone routing alternative and selected that model directly instead of saving Fusion's tier.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The changed interaction awaits the save before applying the model selection, so one persistence operation is on the click path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One configuration edit per explicit tier activation. Rapid edits are serialized per model by SequencerByKey rather than executed concurrently.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Per-model serialization through SequencerByKey; distinct models may proceed independently, but this interaction edits one Fusion model. No concurrency burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The scoped configuration store keeps effective values in memory and suppresses redundant persistence when the selected value is unchanged. A real change updates the scoped storage bucket and mirrors the profile-global configuration.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that one save is newly reached for this interaction; high that it is bounded and coalesced against no-op persistence.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Storage latency varies by platform, but the operation is fixed-cardinality, user-initiated, serialized, and required to persist the newly selected tier semantics.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The newly reached boundary is a single bounded persistence operation necessary for the changed selection behavior, not fan-out or repeated background work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Naming HydraFusion responses in response footers
Scenarios.CriticalPath: When response details are finalized, the handler resolves the in-memory Fusion model and derives the provider tier label before formatting footer text.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One lookup per completed response whose runtime reports a HydraFusion response model; schema scan cost scales with one model's configuration property count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous formatting within response-detail creation; no queue or parallel work is added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Language-model metadata is obtained from the existing turn model lookup/cache. No network fetch or cache invalidation is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the transitive path reaches only metadata lookup, localization, and string formatting.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Schema size and response frequency vary, but each response performs only a small in-memory scan.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Provider-tier naming adds bounded in-memory work per completed response.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 18 changed files and all diff pages. Traced chat notification generation/rendering, activity updates, model-picker render/hover paths, tier persistence, and response-footer formatting. The PR mostly removes serialization and rendering; its only newly reached persistence boundary is one serialized, no-op-suppressed save per explicit tier choice, which is not a material performance regression.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
